schedule.activity: Understand the rider, source data and service day
Connect to Forge and write an acceptance scenario
Build and inspect the single-worker loop
Implement task readiness, claims and isolated copies
Run two workers and test their patches together
Review a project lesson and implement retrieval
Run and inspect the matched follow-up builds
Evaluate frozen builds and diagnose the UTC defect
Reproduce a result and publish the release decision

slides.title:
Build a transit app
with a team of coding agents
slides.notes: The department and deadline are fictional. The schedule records are real public MBTA data. Participants build a bounded software factory; we do not claim to reproduce an unattended production engineering organization. The single session includes three breaks. The extra time is for tracing one concrete input through the implementation, writing the coordinator and explaining the recorded failures.
slides.concept: Build a transit app with a team of coding agents

slides.title: Your team needs a departures board
slides.notes: Start with the person using the software. Ask what could make a plausible-looking board wrong. Listen for wrong date, wrong stop, missing departures and misleading times. No model or agent count appears before the product is clear.
slides.concept: Your team needs a departures board

slides.title: Here is the application we want to deliver
slides.notes: This is a real capture of the reference implementation, not a model outcome. Participants will inspect the app their workers actually produce. Call out the selected Park Street platform, midnight on November 29, and first scheduled departure at 00:08. The next slides explain why that train belongs to November 28 service.
slides.concept: Here is the application we want to deliver

slides.title: The inputs are public transit records
slides.notes: Open the notebook data receipt and read its archive date and checksum. Do not describe the small teaching subset as the complete MBTA system. MBTA describes its feed at https://github.com/mbta/gtfs-documentation/blob/master/reference/gtfs.md . Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: The inputs are public transit records

slides.title: Start with the row for the platform
slides.notes: Keep the same trip visible through the next three slides. Read the actual identifiers aloud once. The product uses these joins, not an LLM guess about the next train. Ask which table must tell us whether this trip runs on Thanksgiving. Timeline spacing is illustrative; timestamps are actual. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: Start with the row for the platform

slides.title: Join the trip to its service calendar
slides.notes: The service ID is a join key. The active dates come from the calendar and exception records. Explain that calendar_dates overrides the weekly rule. This is a historical snapshot and fixed test date, not today’s schedule. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: Join the trip to its service calendar

slides.title: Keep the service date and boarding date
slides.notes: Ask the room to name the two different dates before revealing the timestamp. The train is eight minutes after the next midnight. Explain why hour modulo 24 without carrying the day loses information.
slides.concept: Keep the service date and boarding date

slides.title: The last train can belong to yesterday’s service
slides.notes: This is an actual retained row: trip 63926435, stop 70076, departure_time 24:08:00, stop_sequence 150, ThanksgivingDay service, headsign Alewife. The civil timestamp is 2024-11-29T00:08:00-05:00. Ask what a parser restricted to 0..23 hours would do. The rule must survive between components. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: The last train can belong to yesterday’s service

slides.title: Convert elapsed service time into a timestamp
slides.notes: Explain the datetime origin, timezone and timedelta separately. This example has no daylight-saving transition; it does not replace the full GTFS time specification. The learners write the acceptance check, while the coding worker implements the general query.
slides.concept: Convert elapsed service time into a timestamp

slides.title: Check the joined behavior, not just the parser
slides.notes: These deliberate mutations test the participant’s assertion. They are local examples, not recorded agent mistakes. Explain why a checker that always returns True would pass the first example and fail to teach anything.
slides.concept: Check the joined behavior, not just the parser

slides.title: Turn the brief into checks
slides.notes: These are requirements for our product, not a claim that the initial code fails them. Show the concrete acceptance inputs and expected outputs in the notebook. Final cases stay outside the coding-worker context until the versions are frozen.
slides.concept: Turn the brief into checks

slides.title: A software factory needs a way to finish work
slides.notes: Software factory is a broad term. This slide states the operational meaning we implement. It includes specification, coordination, verification and release. It is not simply a chat room with several role prompts.
slides.concept: A software factory needs a way to finish work

slides.title: Add the task board and two workers
slides.notes: Click once to reveal workers, once to reveal integration, once to reveal the checked lesson. Solid arrows show code or execution flow. The dashed arrow identifies reviewed evidence. The diagram is explanatory, not a recorded run.
slides.concept: Add the task board and two workers

slides.title: Two workers means two contexts around the same model
slides.notes: The worker is a Python loop plus model requests and allowed tools. Two workers do not mean training two new models. Model settings match across the sequential and parallel builds. The comparison asks what the coordination design changes for this task.
slides.concept: Two workers means two contexts around the same model

slides.title: Your project contains the experiment
slides.notes: Keep the distinction between agents sharing project records and attendees sharing credentials. The latter does not happen. The notebook has an adjustable inference allowance; notebook compute is billed separately. Opening the notebook does not start agents.
slides.concept: Your project contains the experiment

slides.title: Connect and inspect the source data
slides.notes: Do not ask participants to paste a key into a code cell. Hosted authentication comes from their own account. Locally use wandb login. Access checks should distinguish a writable project from inference entitlement. The workshop list in the README links to the current native Transit template. If copying is unavailable, use its notebook source/import fallback; do not send attendees to the reference app.
slides.concept: Connect and inspect the source data

exercise.inspect: Send my first Agent Lens trace

slides.title: Record the operation that you just ran
slides.notes: Identify the name, inputs, actual result and time boundaries. Participants add or edit the attribute in the full notebook function and find it in their own setup span. This operation reads the teaching dataset, so it does not spend inference allowance.
slides.concept: Record the operation that you just ran

slides.title: Write the after-midnight acceptance check
slides.name: acceptance-exercise
slides.notes: The scenario is written by the participant and later runs on the integrated app. It is public development evidence, not a hidden final answer. Show how a plausible train list can still use the wrong service day.
slides.concept: Write the after-midnight acceptance check

slides.title: One worker still needs a complete loop
slides.notes: Start with the familiar single-agent harness. Multiple agents do not remove the need for correct tool observation handling, explicit stopping and independent checks. Model settings stay fixed in the comparisons. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: One worker still needs a complete loop

slides.title: Give the worker the task it is allowed to solve
slides.notes: Explain each input before editing: task is the approved contract, sources are the current worker copy, lessons are explicitly retrieved project memory. This excerpt shows the fields that matter; follow the notebook function signature for the executable implementation.
slides.concept: Give the worker the task it is allowed to solve

slides.title: The first action reads the assigned file
slides.notes: This is an explanatory sequence using the implemented tool contract, not an additional live execution. Keep model, Python tool and observation separate. A model choosing read_file is not the same thing as Python executing it.
slides.concept: The first action reads the assigned file

slides.title: The edit includes the version it was based on
slides.notes: Explain optimistic conflict detection: before_sha256 identifies the old file, while the returned hash identifies the new one. A rejected write should produce an observation that the next request can inspect.
slides.concept: The edit includes the version it was based on

slides.title: Run the checks against the changed files
slides.notes: The board clears the old test receipt when a file changes. The current files are what run in a child Python process. That process has restricted imports, a timeout and no inherited Forge credentials; it is reviewed code execution, not a security sandbox.
slides.concept: Run the checks against the changed files

slides.title: Return the tool result to the worker
slides.notes: This participant function controls actual tool dispatch. The runtime supplies bounded file, edit, test and task operations. It records the returned result independently. An unknown action must raise an error rather than invoke arbitrary code.
slides.concept: Return the tool result to the worker

slides.title: Append the actual observation to the next request
slides.notes: The agent action has already been appended as an assistant message. The following user message supplies the observation, any directed messages and remaining action count. The runtime records actual tool execution independently of the learner’s return value. Do not add a second model call here.
slides.concept: Append the actual observation to the next request

slides.title: Finish submits a patch for review
slides.notes: Point out the status change to review. Human review and integration remain separate. If a worker reaches its action limit without this tested completion, the unfinished file is retained as evidence, not silently merged.
slides.concept: Finish submits a patch for review

slides.title: Run one worker before adding a team
slides.name: worker-exercise
slides.notes: Allow participants to read a diff before accepting anything. The tool event and test output must be saved even when the worker fails. A recorded failure is an optional teaching example, not a required live outcome.
slides.concept: Run one worker before adding a team

exercise.run: Run one worker on the first feature

slides.title: A trace should answer what changed and why
slides.notes: Open the participant’s real trace rather than a made-up dashboard image. Each model request, tool action, failed check and handoff should be attributable to a worker and build. Trace export can be retried without rerunning the model.
slides.concept: A trace should answer what changed and why

slides.title: Inspect the worker’s test in Agent Lens
slides.notes: Open the actual conversation link. The record proves that the presentation worker read and edited a file and ran a passing component check. It does not prove the whole app works. The sibling query worker exhausted its output budget in this rehearsal; preserve that failed attempt. Do not turn one passing span into a completed product claim.
slides.concept: Inspect the worker’s test in Agent Lens

slides.title: The request has a size limit even when files are saved
slides.notes: Explain why storing a complete file is different from resending it with every action. R5 still hit a bound after a long write, so this policy is not a guarantee that any generated module will fit. Do not imply that a higher output allowance fixes an oversized input.
slides.concept: The request has a size limit even when files are saved

slides.title: Break until 1:45
slides.notes: Ten-minute break, 1:35–1:45. Use the read-only monitor to find participants who requested help. Do not treat missing progress as failure.
slides.concept: Break until 1:45

slides.title: Choose work that can happen independently
slides.notes: The workers own query.py and presentation.py. The query returns the agreed departure records. The display consumes that interface. Use the actual notebook contract to see exactly which fields are required. Click to expose the join, then the whole-product check. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: Choose work that can happen independently

slides.title: Ready means its prerequisites passed
slides.notes: Completed means accepted completion with saved output, not a worker’s progress narration. The local check should reject a task with an unmet dependency. The precise notebook record fields may include richer status metadata; preserve those contracts.
slides.concept: Ready means its prerequisites passed

slides.title: Both workers can see a pending task
slides.notes: Use the local two-thread fixture, not a theoretical timing claim. Ask learners what changes if both read at the same time. A polite prompt does not make two Python operations atomic.
slides.concept: Both workers can see a pending task

slides.title: A separate check and write permits two owners
slides.notes: The controlled race uses a barrier to reproduce the condition. This two-owner outcome measures coordination code, not model intelligence. Show the broken if-pending then set-owner snippet in the notebook.
slides.concept: A separate check and write permits two owners

slides.title: One short transaction assigns one owner
slides.notes: The same two local threads now have one successful claim. The other gets a not-ready or already-claimed error. Holding the lock for the entire model call would serialize the work and block other claims.
slides.concept: One short transaction assigns one owner

slides.title: Keep the model call outside the claim transaction
slides.notes: This is simplified teaching code; the actual store raises FactoryStop and also records dispatch identity, source and timing. Do not instruct participants to replace the store with this excerpt. The required code change is claim_task in the notebook.
slides.concept: Keep the model call outside the claim transaction

slides.title: Make dependencies control the workers
slides.name: tasks-exercise
slides.notes: Do not solve the race with a prompt asking agents to be careful. Claiming must be atomic in the shared task store. Let two local attempts contend for one task in the free exercise.
slides.concept: Make dependencies control the workers

slides.title: Separate working copies protect unfinished changes
slides.notes: This is a practical reason for independent workspaces, not a guarantee that the generated code is safe. Reviewed local code runs with bounded tools and time limits. Remote Sandboxes remain optional and require their own access. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: Separate working copies protect unfinished changes

slides.title: Each worker starts from the same source
slides.notes: Separate working files do not imply separate authority to change every file. Keep the common starting version visible. This is diagrammatic code flow, not a claim that all future tasks are independent.
slides.concept: Each worker starts from the same source

slides.title: Each task can edit only its assigned module
slides.notes: Point out which files are readable and which are editable. Both task contracts name the same return schema. The worker cannot repair a failing test by changing the evaluator.
slides.concept: Each task can edit only its assigned module

slides.title: Integration checks the patches against their base
slides.notes: Explain why different files still need a combined test: both modules can disagree about a field or timezone. The hash guards against stale file replacement; it does not prove the interface is correct.
slides.concept: Integration checks the patches against their base

slides.title: Run the ready tasks with two workers
slides.notes: Keep the concurrency at two for the core exercise. More workers is an optional later experiment. Do not change model or total budget between comparisons and then attribute a difference only to coordination.
slides.concept: Run the ready tasks with two workers

exercise.run: Run the ready tasks with two workers

slides.title: Read the timeline as work and waiting
slides.notes: Ask which task is on the critical path. Parallel work can reduce elapsed time while increasing aggregate model cost. Queue time, execution time and integration time belong in separate fields.
slides.concept: Read the timeline as work and waiting

slides.title: Find both submitted patches before integration
slides.notes: This is a checkpoint at 2:40, not a break. Integration starts at 2:45. If one worker is unfinished, keep that outcome and inspect the available record rather than inventing a completed patch.
slides.concept: Save the checkpoint before the break

slides.title: Review a patch before it enters the product
slides.notes: The user explicitly approved human review of task contracts and patches. Keep the actual diff visible next to its test output. Do not represent a review decision as an executed version until integration really runs. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: Review a patch before it enters the product

slides.title: Test the combined departures board
slides.notes: Show the combined source identity and acceptance output. If integration fails, preserve it and diagnose the failure before another edit. The facilitator can use the recorded controlled example if the live patches happen to work.
slides.concept: Test the combined departures board

slides.title: An integration error can cross a correct boundary
slides.notes: Do not claim the current agents made this error unless its execution record shows it. This example explains why tests at component boundaries matter. The repair may be to code, task contract, tests or a combination.
slides.concept: An integration error can cross a correct boundary

slides.title: Use the local preview to follow a returned row
slides.notes: If a live build is wrong, keep the output visible and name the failed requirement. The prepared reference continuation appears only if neither initial build passes development integration; it is labeled and never replaces live results.
slides.concept: Use the local preview to follow a returned row

slides.title: Break until 3:20
slides.notes: Twenty-minute break, 3:00–3:20. Resume the same project. Do not change source or model settings to make the live result match the prepared example.
slides.concept: Break until 3:20

slides.title: Shared memory needs something worth sharing
slides.notes: Connect memory to a specific integration incident or verified behavior. Transcripts record what happened. A lesson is an interpretation intended to help a future task. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: Shared memory needs something worth sharing

slides.title: Check the lesson before another agent relies on it
slides.notes: Click to reveal approved memory, then the fresh worker using it. A lesson can describe a successful pattern as well as a failure. Keep claims and verified observations distinct.
slides.concept: Check the lesson before another agent relies on it

slides.title: Write a rule with a test attached
slides.notes: Do not present this as a measured memory success. Explain scope: a rule about schedule times does not mean every display field should print hour 25. Keep the contract version, source evidence and review state visible.
slides.concept: Write a rule with a test attached

slides.title: A saved note is not automatically accepted
slides.notes: The examples are illustrative records matching the retrieval schema, not four observations from R5. Ask which one a fresh worker should receive and which fields justify that choice.
slides.concept: A saved note is not automatically accepted

slides.title: First exclude the unchecked interpretation
slides.notes: The agent can propose a lesson. The participant checks its evidence and writes the accepted rule. This gate reduces propagation of guesses; it cannot guarantee the rule is correct in every context.
slides.concept: First exclude the unchecked interpretation

slides.title: Then check the applicable contract version
slides.notes: Do not compare source_revision to the current code fingerprint. A lesson may be relevant to new code while citing an earlier version. The accepted contract version is the applicability check.
slides.concept: Then check the applicable contract version

slides.title: Finally match the task’s scope and tags
slides.notes: select_memories performs these checks. No vector database is needed for this small project record. Let a participant explain why status alone would retrieve too much.
slides.concept: Finally match the task’s scope and tags

slides.title: Save a lesson supported by an execution
slides.name: memory-exercise
slides.notes: Participants must inspect the evidence rather than approve an agent summary blindly. The retrieval function affects the later actual worker request. A directory listing is not proof that a worker read a lesson.
slides.concept: Save a lesson supported by an execution

exercise.optional: Ask the agent to propose a lesson

slides.title: Inspect the memory read, then its effect
slides.notes: This is the trace-to-behavior chain. A citation or read event establishes consultation, not that the memory caused an improvement. The matched follow-up comparison is what tests that question.
slides.concept: Inspect the memory read, then its effect

slides.title: Find the last direct train between two stops
slides.notes: The follow-up asks for the last direct train between two retained stations, including arrival after midnight, a no-direct-service result and an itinerary download. Each branch uses two workers. Both branches execute; no prerecorded result is substituted for one side. This small paired example teaches the method. One pair cannot establish repeatability or general superiority. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: Find the last direct train between two stops

slides.title: Start both follow-ups from the same release
slides.notes: Each build has two workers. The coordinator invokes the two builds in order, while each build may run its two workers concurrently. Do not describe the two conditions as synchronized or simultaneous. Compare saved initial fingerprints.
slides.concept: Start both follow-ups from the same release

slides.title: Keep both sets of patches and checks
slides.notes: The specification, starting code, fixed research model, limits and tool implementation are held the same. The lesson cannot be edited after inspecting the first outcome and still count as a matched pair.
slides.concept: Keep both sets of patches and checks

slides.title: The follow-up returns a journey, not a list of guesses
slides.notes: Explain the function inputs and two valid output shapes. The retained dataset is small, so None concerns this schedule subset. It is not a statement that no real-world route exists. The renderer cannot invent a trip when the query returns None.
slides.concept: The follow-up returns a journey, not a list of guesses

slides.title: Run both versions of the follow-up feature
slides.notes: Keep memory fixed during this matched comparison. Do not edit it after seeing the no-memory result and call the pair controlled. If budget or infrastructure prevents a branch from finishing, retain a missing result and label the pair incomplete.
slides.concept: Run both versions of the follow-up feature

exercise.run: Run both versions of the follow-up feature
exercise.review: I reviewed the no-lesson and shared-lesson patches

slides.title: The factory has two kinds of state
slides.notes: This is the distinction between a task ledger and learning. Neither requires sharing a giant conversation among all workers. Both need durable records, clear identities and bounded retrieval. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: The factory has two kinds of state

slides.title: Find where the lesson entered the request
slides.notes: If no explicit read_memory action is present, distinguish the initial read_shared_memory selection from an agent-initiated read. Do not claim peer messaging unless the saved events contain it. The R5 workers were coordinated through task records and supplied lessons.
slides.concept: Find where the lesson entered the request

slides.title: Keep a stopped worker’s files and error
slides.notes: Use Recover stopped work only after confirming the earlier execution stopped. A request with an uncertain outcome remains conservatively charged. A bound error is not fixed merely by clicking again. The six-hour schedule includes time to interpret an incomplete build, not unlimited retries.
slides.concept: Keep a stopped worker’s files and error

slides.title: Break until 4:55
slides.notes: Ten-minute break, 4:45–4:55. Stop adding features. The final comparison must include failed or incomplete branches.
slides.concept: Break until 4:55

slides.title: Evaluate the product and the process separately
slides.notes: Avoid a composite score that conceals these tradeoffs. The saved product rows are matched across versions. Missing builds or evaluations remain missing, not silently dropped or converted to ordinary task failures. Repeated task claims include explicit recovery; overlapping reasoning and semantically duplicated code are not measured. Coverage is separate from passed-case rate.
slides.concept: Evaluate the product and the process separately

slides.title: A scenario is an input and an expected behavior
slides.notes: This is a compact teaching excerpt, not the complete final acceptance scorer. Explain why sorting the identifiers before comparing would hide an ordering defect. Failed execution is not equivalent to a valid empty departure list.
slides.concept: A scenario is an input and an expected behavior

slides.title: Compare the frozen builds on matching cases
slides.name: evaluate-exercise
slides.notes: Final grading happens after the build choices freeze. Evaluation Tables Preview uses the working Weave-backed publication path. If publication fails, inspect the notebook rows and retry publication only; do not rerun model work.
slides.concept: Compare the frozen builds on matching cases

slides.title: Read one comparison row before the average
slides.notes: Use one scenario to explain the matching inputs, actual outputs and pass criteria before opening the native comparison on the next slide. Keep its source URL and recorded rehearsal identity visible.
slides.concept: Read one comparison row before the average

slides.title: Compare the same departures in Forge
slides.notes: Actual native Evaluation Tables Preview, verified in a signed-out browser. The saved workspace contains two frozen first-release builds and ten matching scenarios, with all twenty underlying evaluation rows read back. This image does not represent the R4 memory followups, which were incomplete. Open a prediction cell and inspect the service date before treating a matching average as sufficient evidence.
slides.concept: Compare the same departures in Forge

slides.title: The faster build missed two final cases
slides.notes: These are final native scores from R5, a separate engineering rehearsal after context compaction changed. All 56 scenario rows are represented. The first builds passed five public development checks each, but the two-worker final product passed only eight of ten reserved scenarios. Do not treat the earlier R4 native screenshot as this R5 comparison. Builder elapsed excludes human review and integration. Actual provider request counts were 8, 12, 5 and 5 respectively. The no-memory query reached its input bound after writing; the memory query exhausted its output allowance. Both stopped before query tests; presentation was retained unchanged. The lesson proposal cost an additional $0.00143474. Total observed inference was $0.06635800 across 31 provider requests, with zero unknown usage. This single pair cannot establish a general speed or memory effect. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: The faster build missed two final cases

slides.title: Open the two failing rows in the final comparison
slides.notes: Use the actual saved native view. The bottom two rows show the query and integrated application cases. Both select 63919613 in the solo output and 63919759 in the team output. The screenshot is preserved; numbered annotations sit beside the relevant fields. Capture provenance is in notes/r5-capture-receipt.json.
slides.concept: Open the two failing rows in the final comparison

slides.title: A timezone assumption selected the wrong train
slides.notes: The failed cases were departures/utc-input and integrated/departures/utc-input. The two-worker query anchored GTFS service-day midnight to the caller’s timezone. It selected a service-clock 23:03 trip rather than the expected 18:03 Eastern departure after a 23:00 UTC request. The solo query preserved the fixed feed timezone for this historical subset. These are two checks of one defect, not two independent bugs. Both failed follow-up query edits left this earlier bug in place. Ask participants which contract or test they would add before another build. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: A timezone assumption selected the wrong train

slides.title: Interpret the request as one instant
slides.notes: Recorded R5 case: departures/utc-input. This is a same-instant conversion. The feed clock defines the origin of GTFS elapsed service time; the caller is allowed to express the request using another offset. The paired clock positions show matching instants, with nonuniform spacing for legibility. The third position is five hours after the expected departure.
slides.concept: Interpret the request as one instant

slides.title: The team used the caller’s clock for service time
slides.notes: Recorded behavior, not a hypothesized defect. The team anchored service-day midnight to the request timezone. This changed the chosen record, not only its formatted text. Inspect the source and actual prediction beside the expected row. The paired clock positions show matching instants, with nonuniform spacing for legibility. The third position is five hours after the expected departure.
slides.concept: The team used the caller’s clock for service time

slides.title: The renderer carried the same wrong trip into the board
slides.notes: The independent suite checks both the query and the complete application. Avoid describing these correlated cases as two independent coding errors. Learners should propose a public UTC-input regression case for a future experiment, after retaining the current outcome. The paired clock positions show matching instants, with nonuniform spacing for legibility. The third position is five hours after the expected departure.
slides.concept: The renderer carried the same wrong trip into the board

slides.title: Neither follow-up completed the query change
slides.notes: Without memory: oversized input after a saved write. With memory: output allowance exhausted before a complete first action. Both query tasks stopped before testing. The existing query remained; these outcomes do not establish that shared memory caused either failure. Visual revision: follow the same named record across the reveal; all illustrative source edits are labeled. Read the caption before opening the matching notebook exercise.
slides.concept: Neither follow-up completed the query change

slides.title: More workers can still produce more waiting
slides.notes: Primary sources: Claude Code agent-team docs, Google Research scaling-agent-systems study and Anthropic compiler report. Do not import their performance numbers as a forecast for this model or task.
slides.concept: More workers can still produce more waiting

slides.title: Choose a release using the saved checks
slides.notes: The release is a versioned workshop artifact, not an automatic public service deployment. Agent-generated recommendations do not bypass required checks. Preserve previous versions for reproduction and rollback.
slides.concept: Choose a release using the saved checks

slides.title: Publish the version you can reproduce
slides.name: release-exercise
slides.notes: Use the last half-hour for reproduction, release and a short explanation. R5 supports releasing the one-worker departures board. Failed required checks block the follow-up. The output is an artifact and Report, not automatic production deployment.
slides.concept: Publish the version you can reproduce

exercise.run: Publish this release and its evidence

slides.title: Reload the selected app and repeat one case
slides.notes: This is a local inference-free reproduction. It shows that the delivered source and data yield the saved behavior. It is not a rerun of the stochastic coding agents. Verify one row, not merely that the app opens.
slides.concept: Reload the selected app and repeat one case

slides.title: Explain one result to another participant
slides.notes: Give participants two minutes each. The person explaining should control the notebook and open the relevant record. The facilitator should not take the keyboard or supply the conclusion.
slides.concept: Explain one result to another participant

slides.title: Take the coordination code to your own project
slides.notes: Ask each person for one suitable feature, one prerequisite, one acceptance check and one durable project rule from their own team. ARIA is outside the measured comparison and may require additional access.
slides.concept: Take the coordination code to your own project

slides.title: Worked answer: select ready tasks
slides.name: tasks-answer
slides.notes: Use the exact notebook task schema. This answer explains the readiness rule; the claim transaction belongs to the supplied store interface. A separate read followed by an unlocked write allows two workers to claim the same task.
slides.concept: Worked answer: select ready tasks
